newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha edges up with crude, arbitrage debated.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha edges up with crude, arbitrage debated.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices edged higher on Wednesday after crude oil rallied and traders debated whether the arbitrage to the U.S. was now open, and whether that was bullish for European prices.
But the NWE market was still seen relatively balanced for the rest of the month with end-users comfortable and two Russian cargoes of about 8,000-10,000 tonnes expected to arrive.
"I think it's a balanced market," said one broker. "Buyers are still fairly relaxed and comfortable about supply."
A 35,000 tonne Greek cargo was confirmed sold this week at $232-$233 for delivery to Houston by the end of the month.
That prompted talk that the arbitrage was open and further supplies may be drained to the U.S.

But one trader said he did not think the arbitrage was "fully open" to ship cargoes across the Atlantic for a profit, and the Greek cargo may have been sent to the U.S. because it could not be sold in NWE.
"It's rather dangerous at the moment to speculate on the window," he said.
He said the spread between the U.S. and Rotterdam has to be about $5-$7 to make money on the arbitrage, and it did not appear to be that wide at the moment.
He was also watching the U.S. spot propane market where prices rallied on Tuesday on the back of forecasts for below-normal temperatures in many U.S. regions.
"It's up and down and it was open yesterday and we will have to wait and see for today," a broker said.
Dec swaps rose $3 to $223/$224 with Jan $6 behind at $217/$218 and Feb $5.50 backwardated to Jan at $211.50/$212.50.
